name: Money

subjectOf.text: Bitcoin proved that a decentralized digital representation of value is possible, but it is not efficient enough for wide use because the rest of a decentralized economic environment does not yet exist around it.
subjectOf.abstract: Bitcoin proved it was possible to create a decentralized digital representation of value. Because this proof of concept technology doesn't have the rest of a decentralized eco- nomic environment to exist in, it is not efficient enough to use widely.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Eight Institutions for the Evolution of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782205
scope_conditions: Bitcoin as a proof of concept lacking a surrounding decentralized economy

subjectOf.text: Against the objection that the correspondence principle should make quantum effects vanish at macro scales, the paper holds that quantum properties scale up through designed technologies such as money and so affect the economy as a whole.
subjectOf.abstract: proponents of quantum economics maintain that quantum properties can scale up through designed technologies like money, affecting the economy as a whole
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Quantum Economy and Tokenomics (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4900878
scope_conditions: requires designed technologies such as money that transmit micro level effects upward

subjectOf.text: Record protection reaches agents by the deferrable share of their objective rather than by their interest in money, and it applies only when the objective holds enough deferrable value, the relevant quantities can be bounded, and detected resistance produces the forfeitures Proposition 3 assumes; even then it offsets intrinsic control value and expiring value only up to a displayed bound, beyond which record protection alone does not make compliance optimal.
subjectOf.abstract: Should intelligent agents have legal rights? This Article sets that question aside and asks a smaller one that matters more in practice. An intelligent agent that earns a reputation record has something to lose.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Should an Intelligent Agent Have Legal Rights? (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7596939
scope_conditions: the relevant quantities can be bounded
detected resistance produces the forfeitures Proposition 3 assumes
offsets intrinsic control and expiring value only up to the displayed bound
